methodological_questions: Does a within-game change of the offensive five shift shot mix beyond what shooter identity alone explains?
Can the apparent shot-mix shift be separated from mechanical changes in who takes shots?
Are substitution-based contrasts confounded by game state, coach response, and fatigue?
Is the design powered for small shot-mix shifts given the available possession counts?
Are derived play-type labels reliable enough to serve as outcomes or controls?

historical_evidence.finding: PULL_UP exposure-effect diagnostics. With lineup fixed effects the slope holding shot fixed was -0.0255 (0.0061); without lineup FE it was -0.0063 (0.0036); placebo on other play types was -0.0075 (0.0017). The record attributes the apparent effect to a shooter-level confound (failure mechanism C_artifact, limited by LIM:confounding; risks CONFOUNDING and PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE). Sample and power recorded as NOT_RECORDED.

Opponent lineup adaptation: shot mix when the opposing rim big is off the floor. Recorded results (CHT-075 and TMP-020) include DRIVE +0.82pp (SE 0.25), POST_UP +0.43pp (SE 0.18), 3PA -1.79pp (SE 0.31), rim <=4ft +0.12pp (SE about 0.30), and PPP +0.008 (SE 0.007). The record's chat verdict is WEAK/SMALL and it is limited by LIM:small_sample (risk SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER). CHT-075 used N=1.07M possessions. This concerns the defensive side, not changes in the offensive five.

Defensive in-game adaptation to repeated play type (exposure slope). League-wide within-game slope was -0.0019 PPP per exposure (SE 0.0019); across-game +0.0004 (SE 0.0015). Only PULL_UP survived Holm (-0.0243, SE 0.0061, holm 0.0004). Team-trait split-half r was +0.008 and season-to-season r was +0.037. Limited by insufficient exposure, label or classification error, and low measurement reliability.

Observed on-ball defensive scheme labels (ORL-DET G1). Only 14.9% (DET, 10 of 67) and 3.3% (ORL, 2 of 60) of on-ball possessions received confident labels. The switches_on field was unpopulated in the NBA matchups feed. Verdict: failed_gate, limited by label error and small sample.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Attributing a play-type exposure decline to defensive adaptation, using lineup fixed effects and holding shot fixed
failed_approaches.why: The effect shrank from -0.0255 to -0.0063 when lineup FE were removed, and the same-shooter placebo on other play types was of similar size (-0.0075). The record concludes shooter-level confounding (C_artifact).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Detecting sub-1pp shot-mix shifts from opposing-big absence
failed_approaches.why: Estimates were small and imprecise (rim share SE 0.295). The PPP effect had t=+1.1. The record's verdict is WEAK/SMALL and it will not carry a paper (LIM:small_sample).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Measuring within-game defensive adaptation to repeated play types
failed_approaches.why: Most play types gave near-zero slopes with wide intervals. Only PULL_UP survived correction, and its validity is undermined by the artifact finding in SF-TMP-009. Team-trait reliability was very low (split-half r +0.008).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Labeling on-ball defensive coverage (DROP/ICE/SWITCH) from the matchups feed
failed_approaches.why: Label rates were very low and switches_on was not populated, so the question was judged unanswerable with this data (A_unanswerable).

evidence_establishes: Shooter-level confounding can produce an apparent exposure or personnel effect that disappears or shrinks when shooter identity is controlled (SF-TMP-009). Any test of the offensive-five question must include a same-shooter placebo.
Effects of the size typical in this project's shot-mix work (sub-1pp to about 2pp) are hard to detect with the available sample unless the contrast is tightly designed (SF34, SF38).

Derived defensive scheme labels are not reliable at usable rates from this feed (SF-APPS-058), so derived play-type or coverage labels should not serve as primary outcomes or controls without validation.
No retrieved record tests whether changing the offensive five moves shot mix. The question is therefore open.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether changing the offensive five moves shot mix in these seasons. No retrieved record studies offensive-five changes as the exposure.
The size of any offensive-five effect, or whether the design has power for it. SF-TMP-009 did not record sample and power, and SF34 and SF38 concern other exposures.
Whether the question's premise (that the design can detect personnel effects) holds. The question text presupposes the answer; the retrieved records do not verify it.
Whether substitution timing is exogenous to shot selection in these data. No record examined coach substitution decisions.
own_inferences: Shot mix will almost certainly change when the offensive five changes, because different players take different shots. This mechanical change is not evidence of a personnel effect. The informative estimand is the residual shot-mix change after conditioning on shooter identity and expected shot quality.

Because of this mechanical floor, the phrase 'showing the design can detect personnel effects' is nearly guaranteed by composition and would be a weak test. A valid design must show that the residual, shooter-adjusted shift is nonzero and that placebo contrasts are null.

Substitutions are chosen in response to game state (score, foul trouble, fatigue), so they are probably not random. Controlling for game state and using within-game contrasts with team-by-period fixed effects reduces this risk but does not remove it.

Play-type labels from the graph database are derived from play-by-play outcomes (points, initiator). Using them as outcomes or stratifiers risks outcome-derived labels and leakage, so shot-level fields from the play-by-play should be used directly.
The three seasons (2022-23 to 2024-25) probably differ in pace, rules, and roster construction, so season fixed effects or season-specific estimates are needed.
uncertainties: The retrieved records are about related but distinct questions. No record reports power, effect size, or sample size for offensive-five changes.
Sample sizes for qualifying substitution contrasts are unknown until counted in the data.
The SF38 record is truncated in the retrieval ('[cut; read_family for the full text]'). Its PULL_UP detail was not read in full.
The 'auto_' fields in the records are system-generated classifications; I have reported them as recorded and have not independently verified them.
Whether the substitution_rotation intervals and starters files align exactly with play-by-play clocks is not established by any record.

historical_effect.explanation: Before retrieval, the plan looked like a standard within-game substitution contrast. The retrieved records changed it in three ways. (1) SF-TMP-009 showed that shooter-level confounding can create an apparent personnel-linked effect, so the design must hold shooter identity fixed and include same-shooter placebo outcomes. (2) SF34 and SF38 showed that small shot-mix effects are underpowered here, so the design needs a pre-specified minimum detectable effect and a restricted, high-exposure sample. (3) SF-APPS-058 showed that derived labels are unreliable, so the outcome must come from raw shot-level fields. These changes mean the question should proceed only as a restricted, pre-registered test, not as a general claim.

blocking_constraints.text: Shot mix changes mechanically when shooters change. Without conditioning on shooter identity and expected shot quality, a detected shift would be uninformative about personnel effects.
Substitutions respond to game state and fatigue. Within-game contrasts with game-state controls are needed, and residual confounding remains possible.
Prior shot-mix effects of sub-1pp to about 2pp were underpowered or weak (SF34, SF38). A minimum detectable effect must be computed before analysis.
Derived play-type and coverage labels are unreliable (SF-APPS-058) and may be built from outcomes. Primary outcomes must use raw shot-level fields.

prior_work.summary: None of the retrieved records tests whether changing the offensive five moves shot mix. SF34 and SF38 address defensive-side and exposure questions and are related only in method. SF-TMP-009 is the most relevant methodological warning (shooter-level confound). SF-APPS-058 is relevant to label reliability. The question is therefore not already answered by retrieved work.

risks.text: Different shooters take different shots, so shot mix shifts by construction. A positive result without shooter-level adjustment is not evidence of a personnel effect.
Coach substitution decisions depend on score, foul trouble, and fatigue, which also affect shot selection.
The SF-TMP-009 artifact shows that a same-shooter placebo can reveal confounding. A null placebo is required before a positive effect is interpreted.
Substitutions may follow short-term performance or shot results, producing regression-to-the-mean effects on shot mix.
Effects of the magnitude seen in SF34 and SF38 may be too small for the available swap count, especially after restricting to qualifying contrasts.
Many offensive-five changes involve few possessions, and shot-type cells (3PA, rim, post) are sparse within a single stint.
Team and season trait reliability was very low in SF38 (r about 0.01 to 0.04), so team-level shot-mix tendencies may be unstable outcomes.
Play-type labels derived from the graph database may encode points or shot outcomes, which would leak the outcome into the predictor or stratifier.
Defensive scheme labels were largely unpopulated (SF-APPS-058). Any matchup-based control is unreliable without validation.
Shot-mix tendencies and substitution patterns may shift across 2022-23 to 2024-25, and playoff rotations differ from regular season.
Multiple shot zones, substitution types, and seasons create many comparisons, raising false-positive risk.
Alignment of substitution intervals, starters, and play-by-play clocks can introduce misattributed possessions.

design.estimand: Within-team change in offensive shot-zone distribution (rim, midrange, 3PA share, and expected points per shot) when one offensive player is replaced by another, conditional on shooter identity and expected shot quality, relative to placebo contrasts.
design.unit: Offensive possession, nested in team-game-stint. Contrasts are the 5 possessions before and after a single-player offensive substitution within the same game and period.
design.sample: Regular-season 2022-23, 2023-24, and 2024-25 play-by-play for all teams. Playoffs are excluded from the primary analysis and reserved as a secondary replication. Include only swaps where the entering and exiting players each have a minimum shot count, set in advance.
design.power: Before analysis, simulate the minimum detectable shot-mix shift at 80% power for the qualifying swap count. Report it and treat results below it as uncertain, not null. No power has been established by the retrieved records.
design.controls: Shooter identity fixed effects (run with and without, reporting both). Game-state controls: score margin, period, and clock bins. Team-by-period and season fixed effects. Minutes on floor as a fatigue proxy. Outcomes are raw shot-level fields from play-by-play, not derived play-type labels.
design.falsification: Placebo 1: the same swap contrasts with the outcome replaced by defensive-side shot mix, which should show no offensive personnel effect. Placebo 2: the same-shooter contrast on non-shot possessions (for example turnovers or fouls drawn). Placebo 3: pre-period contrasts (5 possessions before the swap compared with 5 possessions earlier), which should be null. If placebos are nonnull, the primary effect is treated as an artifact.
design.multiplicity: One primary test (shooter-adjusted residual shot mix, 3PA share). Secondary zones and playoff replication are reported under Holm correction across the pre-registered set.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if the shooter-adjusted primary estimate has a 95% CI excluding zero, exceeds the pre-registered minimum detectable effect, and all three placebos are null with CIs including zero. Artifact if the effect is nonnull only without shooter FE, as in SF-TMP-009. Uncertain if power is below the threshold. Rejected only if powered and the primary and placebo estimates are null.
design.data_version: NBA regular-season play-by-play, substitution rotation intervals, starters, and box scores for 2022-23, 2023-24, and 2024-25, as extracted on the pre-registration date (2026-11-02). Derived play-type graph labels are excluded from the primary analysis.

research_concepts: partial possessions and defensive matchup minutes
methodological_questions: Can changing the offensive five detectably shift shot mix in play-by-play data?
What confounders (game state, fatigue, play calling, player quality) threaten a lineup-change design?
Is the design powered and reliable given substitution exposure and derived play-type labels?

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 4 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY
